pages.title: Start here: how the lodge runs

text.text: Pets is the master record: owner, coat, handling and vaccines. Grooming appointments is the grooming table. Boarding stays is the kennel. Incident notes is what you owe every owner: the truth about what happened while you had their pet.
against the vaccine column on each pet: nobody boards or plays in group with an expired record.
Check in each groom on arrival and confirm the cut with the owner.
Check in boarders, write feeding and medication on the stay, and put them in the run listed.
. Move each pet to On the table, then Ready for pickup, and enter the minutes it took. Press
at every shift change and feeds from the stay notes. Anything unusual becomes an Incident note right away; the owner is told before pickup, never at it.
Green means easygoing. Yellow means slow introductions. Orange means a muzzle for nails. Red means no group play.
Every color is set on the pet record once, so every shift and every groomer sees the same warning.
Who is on the grooming table today, who is sleeping over, who arrives this week and whose vaccines are running out.

pages.title: Pricing grooms by coat and time

text.text: A grooming table earns by the hour, not by the dog. Price every service so that a groomer's hour on the table earns at least 60 USD, and charge for the coats that take longer.
add 15 to 30 USD. These coats mat close to the skin and take longest to dry.
a de-shed takes an hour of blowing out. Never shave a double coat short unless the vet asks; it can grow back patchy.
hand stripping is slow work. Price it per hour, not per dog.
Matted coats are a welfare issue as well as a time issue. Tell the owner at drop-off, shave down rather than de-mat if it would hurt, and add a matting fee. Write the conversation on the groom card.
at the end of every groom. The
column divides the price and add-ons by the time. Look at it each week:
Under 55 USD an hour on a service means it is underpriced or the groomer needs help with that coat.
A breed that always runs long, for example a standard poodle in a show clip, deserves its own price.
Cancelled and no-show appointments leave the column blank, so the average stays honest.
Send a reminder by text the day before. A second no-show means a deposit for the next booking. Otis's empty nail-trim slot is the kind of gap that costs a groomer half an hour.
Most coats need a groom every four to eight weeks. Book the next one before the owner leaves; it fills the calendar more reliably than any advertising.
Owners leave their pets with you because they trust you will notice. Every step below exists so that nothing about a boarder depends on one person's memory.

Reserve the run that fits: standard runs for most dogs, large runs for big dogs and siblings, suites for older dogs that need a cot, and the cat condos away from barking. Record nights, nightly rate and any playtime on the stay.

Before a dog boards or joins group play, check three dates on its pet record: rabies, the distemper combination and bordetella for kennel cough. Cats need rabies and their own combination vaccine. The
column turns to Update needed the day anything lapses, and Otis is the example: his kennel cough shot ran out, so he cannot stay until the owner brings a new record.
Weigh the dog and write the weight on the stay page.
Take the food in labeled bags; write the amounts on the stay as the owner says them.
Medication goes in the locked box with the pet's name on it. Tick
Ask for a phone number that will answer during the trip.
Feed from the stay notes and record anything not eaten. Two skipped meals in a row is an incident note and a call to the owner.
Pets marked red for handling never go in group play.
Walk, clean the run, fresh water, and a few minutes of attention for each boarder.
Bathe long-stay dogs before they go home if the owner asked for it. Press
: it stamps the day they went home. Tell the owner how the stay went, including anything in Incident notes, before you take payment.
